chunks.text: U-Pb dating of zircon constrains emplacement of the carbonatite complex to 386 ± 4 Ma.
The carbonatites consist mainly of calcite, dolomite, apatite and magnetite with elevated rare-earth elements.
Trace-element ratios indicate that the basalts formed in a continental rift setting rather than at a mid-ocean ridge.
Two-pyroxene thermometry gives crystallization temperatures between 980 and 1040 degrees Celsius.
Major elements were measured by X-ray fluorescence, while trace elements were determined using ICP-MS.
Sr-Nd isotope data suggest that the granitic magma was produced by partial melting of ancient continental crust.
The principal ore minerals are chalcopyrite, pyrite and bornite; molybdenite occurs only as an accessory phase.
The measured and indicated resource contains 42 million tonnes of ore at an average copper grade of 0.74 percent.
Most earthquakes in the sequence occurred at depths of 8 to 14 km, with the mainshock hypocenter at 11 km.
The moment magnitude of the mainshock was Mw 6.2 and the largest aftershock reached Mw 5.1.
Lake-water salinity increased from 18 to 27 grams per liter during the 2010–2020 observation period.
The salinity rise is attributed to reduced river inflow and enhanced evaporation during prolonged drought.
Satellite images show that the glacier terminus retreated by an average of 23 meters per year between 1990 and 2020.
Glacier boundaries were mapped from cloud-free Landsat scenes and checked against differential GPS surveys.
Lead concentrations in soils within one kilometer of the smelter exceed the regional background by a factor of twelve.
The proposed remediation combines removal of the most polluted topsoil with phytostabilization using metal-tolerant grasses.
The active layer above permafrost thickened from 0.9 to 1.3 meters over the last fifteen years.
Active-layer thickening correlates with rising summer air temperature and earlier disappearance of seasonal snow.
Hydraulic-head measurements show groundwater flow from the northeastern recharge area toward the river valley.
Tritium and carbon-14 data indicate a mixture of modern recharge and groundwater older than six thousand years.
SO2 emissions rose sharply three days before the eruption, whereas CO2 flux remained nearly constant.
The eruption was preceded by volcanic tremor, summit inflation and a rapid increase in sulfur-dioxide emissions.
Detrital-zircon ages identify the northern craton as the dominant source of the basin sediments.
Cross-bedded sandstone and channel-lag conglomerate record deposition by a braided river system.
